summary: HelioSupport POC: streaming chat completions disconnect/timeout (first token >60s / SSE drops mid-response)
related_confluence_pages: Support Runbook: Streaming/SSE troubleshooting (API Gateway timeouts)
description:
Customer reports intermittent streaming disconnects during HelioSupport POC when using /v1/chat/completions with stream=true. Two patterns observed:

1) Connection drops before first token (TTFT > ~60s). Customer sees client-side timeout / socket hang up.
2) Connection drops mid-stream for longer generations (agent responses > ~700 tokens), causing their UI to show partial answer and then retry.

Impact
- Blocks HelioSupport from validating “stable streaming” requirement for support-agent workflow.
- POC acceptance criteria includes: no streaming drops during normal business hours at target concurrency (10–25) and stable TTFT for typical prompts.

Customer context (POC)
- Workload: support-agent chat; typical inputs include long ticket history + KB snippets.
- Client: Node.js service (fetch/EventSource-style SSE handling) behind a managed egress/proxy.
- Concurrency: 10–25 parallel streams during replay tests.

What we’ve captured so far
- Multiple 499s in gateway logs (client closed request) and upstream timeout indicators during prefill.
- In a subset, first token appears after ~65–90s on 70B model when prompt is large (>10k tokens) and system prompt includes heavy formatting.
- Current gateway idle timeout on streaming path appears to be 60s in prod/us-east (suspected).

Steps to reproduce (Redwood-side)
1. Use model redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct
2. Submit /v1/chat/completions with stream=true
3. Input: large context (10k–16k tokens) + max_tokens ~800–1200
4. Observe: no bytes flushed until first token; connection may be closed at ~60s

Example customer error (from HelioSupport logs)
- "Error: socket hang up" and occasional "ETIMEDOUT" when awaiting first SSE chunk.

Example request identifiers (from Console)
- org: heliosupport-poc
- request_ids: req_01J7H8KQ7Y9ZK2, req_01J7H8M1VQ0P3A

Investigation notes / hypotheses
- Primary: API gateway / load balancer idle timeout is expiring before first token when TTFT exceeds 60s (large prefill + batching).
- Secondary: Customer egress/proxy may enforce its own idle timeout; even if ours is increased, we should emit periodic keepalive bytes or earlier flush.

Immediate mitigations offered to customer (until fix)
- Use smaller model for POC replay (8B) for long-context prompts OR reduce prompt size (truncate ticket history) to keep TTFT <60s.
- Temporarily run stream=false for the longest contexts (customer can show typing indicator based on non-stream response time).
- If using Node fetch: ensure no client timeout <120s; set agent keepAlive; confirm proxy idle timeout.

Links
- Related internal discussion: Slack #customer-success (thread: streaming stability for HelioSupport POC) and #support (June 3–4)
- Fireflies: ff_2025-06-03_heliosupport_poc-checkin.json (POC check-in notes)

Requested outcome
- Increase streaming idle timeout on our gateway OR add SSE keepalive/flush behavior so connections don’t go idle during long prefill.
- Provide customer-facing guidance on recommended timeout settings + prompt/TTFT guardrails for production.
comments: 2025-06-03 (Miguel Santos): Customer saw 6 disconnects across ~120 streaming requests during traffic replay (10–15 concurrency). Most failures happen when prompt includes full ticket thread + 3 KB articles. They need stable streaming to proceed to reference call eligibility later this quarter, but for now it’s a hard POC requirement. Adding Liam + Markus for technical deep dive. Customer is ok with us using their request_ids internally.

2025-06-03 (Liam O'Rourke): Pulled Console traces for req_01J7H8KQ7Y9ZK2. TTFT ~72s on 70B with input_tokens ~14.8k; generation would have started but gateway closed at ~60–61s with no bytes sent. Gateway log shows upstream still computing prefill when client disconnect recorded. This matches idle timeout on streaming path. Next: confirm ingress/NLB timeout setting for /v1/chat/completions stream route in us-east.

2025-06-03 (Markus Klein): Adding note: customer’s app is behind a managed proxy (they mentioned “corporate egress gateway”). Even after we raise our timeouts, they may still need to raise theirs. But first-token gap is on us to mitigate (either earlier flush or longer idle). I’ll align with them on client settings during tomorrow’s call.

2025-06-04 (Liam O'Rourke): Confirmed: prod/us-east streaming route had 60s idle timeout at gateway layer (nginx proxy_read_timeout) + NLB idle 60s. For large prefill workloads, no bytes are flushed until first token, so connections appear idle. Proposed fix: raise to 180s for streaming endpoints + add periodic SSE comment/ping every 15s while waiting for first token. Filed infra change as redwood-infra#2194 for rollout to us-east first.

2025-06-04 (Miguel Santos): Shared interim mitigation with HelioSupport: for their replay test, use 8B model for prompts >8k tokens and cap max_tokens at 700. They can still validate agent UX while we push timeout fix. They confirmed their proxy idle timeout is 90s, and their Node client had a 60s request timeout configured in one service (they’ll bump to 180s).

2025-06-05 (Liam O'Rourke): Deployed config change in prod/us-east: gateway streaming idle timeout increased to 180s; enabled SSE keepalive comments while waiting for first token. Verified in staging with synthetic test: TTFT 95s no longer disconnects; first token delivered and stream completes. Monitoring errors: 499s dropped back to baseline for heliosupport-poc org since deploy. Next: watch for any unintended resource holding; added limit to keepalive only until first token.

2025-06-05 (Miguel Santos): Customer reran replay: 0 disconnects in 200 requests at 15–20 concurrency. They still saw 2 slower TTFT outliers (~110s) but stream stayed connected, which is acceptable for POC as long as it doesn’t drop. They asked if we can recommend “safe” prompt size thresholds; I told them we’ll send guidance based on TTFT observed per model + region.

2025-06-06 (Liam O'Rourke): Closing as Resolved. Root cause: gateway/NLB idle timeout on streaming endpoints combined with long prefill (no bytes flushed until first token). Fix: increased idle timeout + added SSE keepalive until first token. Follow-up: publish a short support note for customers about client/proxy timeouts and TTFT guardrails; consider productizing early flush/heartbeat as a configurable stream option.
